title: Before You Pay ANY Collections...Watch This First
actionable_recommendations: Use a debt negotiation letter from getdisputletters.com or secretcreditletters.com for negotiating debts.
Dispute debts with Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion using a 609-611 letter before negotiating.
Consider hiring a law firm for debt negotiations instead of a negotiator.
Send debt dispute letters via trackable or certified mail to ensure receipt.
claims_requiring_current_verification: Credit report statutes vary by state and can affect how long debts stay on reports.
Some collection agencies may not have the legal transfer documentation required to validate the debt.
Certain states permit debts to remain on credit reports for different lengths of time (e.g., Ohio - 15 years).
intended_organization_or_user: Individuals seeking credit negotiation assistance and education on managing debt.
major_ideas: Debts may be negotiable down to pennies on the dollar, especially older debts.
Communication with creditors should be avoided over the phone to prevent admitting ownership of the debt.
Disputing debts first can sometimes lead to their removal from credit reports without negotiation.
prerequisites: Check local state statutes regarding debt duration on credit reports.
Obtain and submit appropriate identification and documentation when disputing debts.
proposed_workflow: Identify old debts and categorize them for negotiation.
Obtain and send debt dispute letters using proper identification to credit bureaus.
If necessary, attempt to negotiate debts with collection agencies using provided templates.
Consider consulting a law firm if negotiations fail or if legal action is involved.
